function: p. 3-5: Downlink CSI feedback: learnable linear-projection encoder at the user and an L2O decoder with learnable sparse transform at the BS reconstruct the channel.
system: p. 3, 9: FDD massive MIMO, 1024 subcarriers; BS with 32 antennas (COST 2100: 5.3 GHz indoor, 300 MHz outdoor) or 128 (QuaDRiGa indoor); single-antenna user; no RIS.
method: p. 5-10: Learnable linear encoder; decoder with MLP sparse transform and element-wise LSTM learning-to-optimize iterations; end-to-end training with reconstruction MSE (called unsupervised), Adam.
data_channel: p. 9: COST 2100 indoor (5.3 GHz) and outdoor (300 MHz), Nt=32, and QuaDRiGa indoor, 128 antennas; 100,000 training, 30,000 validation, 20,000 test samples.
test_conditions: p. 9, 13: Test on held-out samples of each scenario; trained at compression ratio 1/16 and tested directly at other ratios (Fig. 10); noisy-CSI test, AWGN variance 0.1.
baselines: p. 10, 13: Non-learned ISTA; learned MS4L2O, CsiNet, TransNet, TiLISTA; multi-rate learned SM-CsiNet+ and PM-CsiNet+.
metrics: p. 10: NMSE of the recovered channel; FLOPs and trainable parameters; bit-level NMSE with Lloyd-Max quantization (B bits per element).
complexity: p. 9, 11: Orders O(NaNtM) encoder, O(T_L2O(2C_finv+C_LSTM)) decoder; FLOPs and parameters in Tables II-III, e.g. encoder 0.262 M FLOPs at ratio 1/16 (1.5% of TransNet).
q2_support: p. 13: "The proposed method in Fig. 10 is trained when the compression ratio is 1/16 and directly tested for other settings"
q3_support: p. 10: "ISTA: A classical CS algorithm without learning component"; p. 10: "Among the five learning-based methods, the proposed Csi-L2O scheme achieves the best performance" (CsiNet, TransNet, TiLISTA, MS4L2O; NMSE, Figs. 5-7)
q4_support: p. 9: "the encoder complexity of the proposed Csi-L2O is O(Na Nt M )"; p. 11: "the proposed Csi-L2O only requires 1.5% number of FLOPs of TransNet"
q5_support: p. 9: "following the experimental setting in [9], two types of channel matrices are generated" (the authors generate their own COST 2100 and QuaDRiGa samples; no link to code or data; ref. [43] is only the thop FLOPs counter)
notes: Area 2: CSI compression and feedback. q2 rests only on the multi-rate test (train at 1/16, test at other compression ratios, p. 13); there is no cross-scenario or cross-dataset test, which the paper leaves as future work (p. 14: "the channel distribution in real-world communication systems may differ from the one observed during model training"). q5: COST 2100 and QuaDRiGa are public channel models, but the paper releases no samples or code and states no public dataset, so the reviewer should confirm that generating data with them does not count as a public dataset. The loss the paper calls unsupervised is the reconstruction MSE (p. 6, p. 9).
